assumptions: VecScreen's own blastn parameters and Strong/Moderate/Weak category rules.
The UniVec build named (core or full).
limits: Finds only what UniVec holds; a contaminant missing from it reads as clean.
bio.jane/contract.question: Does this sequence carry vector, adapter, linker or primer contamination from UniVec, and how strong is each match?

description: Screen a nucleotide sequence for vector, adapter, linker and primer contamination against NCBI's UniVec, using VecScreen's own BLASTn parameters and category rules. Reports every match graded Strong/Moderate/Weak plus the short 'suspect origin' stretches NCBI asks to be removed with the vector, and emits both the N-masked sequence and the longest clean region so a pipeline can gate on the result or carry the clean part onward.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

build.description: which UniVec build to search: 'core' is NCBI's curated 3,155-segment subset and is what routine screening should use; 'full' is the complete 6,111-segment set — more sensitive, and more redundant hits.

dust.description: mask low-complexity sequence for SEEDING only (`-dust yes -soft_masking true`): a seed may not START in masked sequence, but an extension may run through it, so a genuine match spanning a repeat is not truncated. Advanced.

gap_extend.description: cost per gapped base (`-gapextend`). Default is NCBI's published VecScreen setting; changing it means the result is no longer VecScreen's. Advanced.

gap_open.description: cost to open a gap (`-gapopen`); a gap of length k costs `gapopen + k * gapextend`. Default is NCBI's published VecScreen setting; changing it means the result is no longer VecScreen's. Advanced.

internal_moderate.description: raw score at or above which an internal match is graded Moderate. Each ladder must stay in order (strong >= moderate >= weak) or the lower rungs become unreachable, and the run is refused rather than graded. Advanced.

internal_strong.description: raw score at or above which an internal match — one that is not terminal — is graded Strong. Each ladder must stay in order (strong >= moderate >= weak) or the lower rungs become unreachable, and the run is refused rather than graded. Advanced.

internal_weak.description: raw score at or above which an internal match is reported at all, as Weak. NCBI leaves a deliberate gap here: an internal match scoring 16-22 is not reportable, because an internal match needs more evidence than a terminal one. Each ladder must stay in order (strong >= moderate >= weak) or the lower rungs become unreachable, and the run is refused rather than graded. Advanced.

min_score.description: lowest raw score worth reporting — VecScreen's weakest reportable match. Lowering it reports more and specifies less. Default is NCBI's published VecScreen setting; changing it means the result is no longer VecScreen's. Advanced.

penalty.description: score for a mismatching base, NEGATIVE (`-penalty`). With reward 1 and penalty −5 only a near-exact stretch can score above the reporting floor, which is what makes VecScreen specific. Default is NCBI's published VecScreen setting; changing it means the result is no longer VecScreen's. Advanced.

reward.description: score for a matching base (`-reward`). Default is NCBI's published VecScreen setting; changing it means the result is no longer VecScreen's. Advanced.

sequence.description: the nucleotide sequence to screen; leave empty to screen the open record. A protein sequence is refused — this is a nucleotide search.

suspect_origin_max.description: length under which a stretch of non-vector sequence stranded between two matches (or between a match and an end) is reported as 'suspect origin' — too short to have come from anywhere trustworthy, so NCBI asks for it to be removed with the vector. Advanced.

terminal_distance.description: how close to an end of the query — or to another reported region — a match must reach to count as terminal and be graded on the lower of the two ladders. NCBI's published value is 25 bases. Advanced.

terminal_moderate.description: raw score at or above which a terminal match is graded Moderate. Each ladder must stay in order (strong >= moderate >= weak) or the lower rungs become unreachable, and the run is refused rather than graded. Advanced.

terminal_strong.description: raw score at or above which a terminal match is graded Strong. A terminal match — one reaching within `terminal_distance` of an end of the query or of another reported region — is believed on less evidence than an internal one, which is why the two ladders differ. Each ladder must stay in order (strong >= moderate >= weak) or the lower rungs become unreachable, and the run is refused rather than graded. Advanced.

terminal_weak.description: raw score at or above which a terminal match is reported at all, as Weak. Below this a terminal match is not reported. Each ladder must stay in order (strong >= moderate >= weak) or the lower rungs become unreachable, and the run is refused rather than graded. Advanced.

ungapped_cutoff.description: lowest ungapped score that sends a seed to gapped extension — blastn’s gap trigger, converted from 27 bits. Default is NCBI's published VecScreen setting; changing it means the result is no longer VecScreen's. Advanced.

word_size.description: exact-match seed length (`-word_size`). A sequence shorter than this cannot be screened at all, and the engine says so. Default is NCBI's published VecScreen setting; changing it means the result is no longer VecScreen's. Advanced.

x_drop_gapped.description: X-drop for the preliminary gapped pass, in score units (`-xdrop_gap`, converted); capped at each seed’s own ungapped score. Default is NCBI's published VecScreen setting; changing it means the result is no longer VecScreen's. Advanced.

x_drop_gapped_final.description: X-drop for the traceback that produces the reported alignment, in score units (`-xdrop_gap_final`, converted). Default is NCBI's published VecScreen setting; changing it means the result is no longer VecScreen's. Advanced.

x_drop_ungapped.description: X-drop for ungapped extension, in score units. It bounds extension; it does not change which alignment is optimal. Default is NCBI's published VecScreen setting; changing it means the result is no longer VecScreen's. Advanced.

name: screen_contamination

cleanSequence.description: the longest stretch carrying no match at all — wire it onward when the screen is a trimming step rather than a gate. Empty when nothing clean is left

contaminatedPct.description: percentage of the query covered by at least one reported match — the slot to gate on numerically

maskedSequence.description: the query with every match and suspect-origin stretch replaced by N — the form NCBI asks a submitter to upload

matches.description: every raw match, one per database record: coordinates, strand, score and the UniVec entry hit

segments.description: the merged contaminated regions, each with its coordinates and category — what the map draws

worst.description: the highest category present — strong | moderate | weak | suspect — or 'clean' when nothing was found. The slot to branch a pipeline on
